assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a new observational window with a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice is a clear, original instrumental and scientific achievement: the discovery of a diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux and, later, evidence for neutrino emission from the Milky Way plane and from specific sources. As an astroparticle experimentalist I regard the detector concept and its realisation as the decisive step, with lasting impact on multi-messenger astronomy.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the IceCube concept and collaboration, Karle was central to detector construction and the discovery analyses, and Spiering represents the long path from Baikal and AMANDA toward large-volume detectors. The listed credit supports a fair three-person configuration, but the full result is the product of a very large collaboration and the roles of early pioneers (for example the DUMAND and Baikal efforts) may be argued differently.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed in several independent channels within IceCube, and the Galactic-plane result is a separate analysis; independent confirmation by other detectors such as KM3NeT or Baikal-GVD is still developing. The interpretation of the individual source associations is still moving, but the core discovery is stable enough that recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Confirmation of the astrophysical flux so far comes largely from one experiment, with other detectors not yet at comparable sensitivity.
The share of credit among Halzen, Karle, Spiering and the pioneers of earlier neutrino telescopes is a judgement I cannot verify independently.
Source identification (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) remains statistically modest, so the prize would rest mainly on the diffuse flux.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle, followed by the experimental demonstration of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene, created a new tunable platform for strongly correlated matter. It is original, clear and has already generated a very large and productive field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald supplied the continuum-model prediction of the magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the decisive experimental observations of correlated insulators and superconductivity. This maps cleanly onto theory plus experiment, though the contributions of other experimental groups and of earlier theoretical work on twisted-layer electronic structure could be argued as well.
assessment.maturity: The main phenomena have been reproduced by multiple groups and the field is mature enough for recognition. Many questions about the nature of the superconducting pairing remain open, but the discovery of the platform does not depend on them.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is unresolved.
Other groups, for example the Columbia and Harvard-linked experimental teams, also made early contributions and the supplied credit may not capture them.
I am outside my own field for the detailed condensed-matter assessment and rely on general knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics established the architecture used for reading out and coupling superconducting qubits and made strong light-matter coupling possible on a chip. The idea is original, the experimental demonstration is clear, and the impact on quantum technology and on fundamental tests of quantum optics is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Blais provided the theoretical proposal, while Wallraff and Schoelkopf realised strong coupling experimentally with Yale colleagues. The credit set supports a theory-plus-experiment configuration, although other Yale co-authors and collaborators in the original work are not on the list and the allocation among them is a question.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed and now standard in many laboratories and in commercial processors. The prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits has already recognised related physics, so the committee would have to judge how distinct this contribution is.
uncertainties: Overlap with already recognised work on superconducting circuits could weigh against a further prize in the same area.
Whether the prize should be framed around cQED itself or around the broader qubit technology is not settled by the supplied evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock combines trapping and interrogation of many atoms without perturbing the transition, which has led to fractional uncertainties beyond the current SI second and to new tests of fundamental physics. The idea is original and the precision-measurement impact is concrete and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove its extension to record accuracy and many-body effects. A two-person prize is natural, though other optical-clock pioneers, especially ion-clock groups, have made adjacent contributions that the supplied credit does not include.
assessment.maturity: Several independent laboratories reproduce and surpass the original performance, and the redefinition of the second is under discussion. Recognition looks timely, particularly as the second may be redefined in the coming years.
uncertainties: Relative weight of lattice clocks and single-ion optical clocks in the overall story is a judgement.
Part of the 2005 and 2012 prize territory concerns related technology, so novelty relative to those prizes needs care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS completed the Standard Model's particle content and is a landmark of detector and accelerator science. The theoretical prediction has been recognised, and the experimental confirmation is one of the clearest discoveries of the century. I know this work well from my CERN background and detector experience.
assessment.attribution: This is the hardest part: the result is the work of two collaborations of thousands. The listed names are leaders and spokespersons, but a prize configuration restricted to three people would be somewhat arbitrary, and the committee would have to decide whether recognising leadership of the experimental effort is fair. Della Negra's omission from my three is a forced choice from a four-name list.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed by two independent experiments and subsequent coupling measurements. Timing is long past maturity, the issue being only attribution rather than evidence.
uncertainties: Attribution among thousands of collaborators and four named leaders cannot be resolved cleanly.
I have a professional connection to CERN-based experimental work, which is not a documented tie to these specific people, but I declare it as relevant background.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed-light injection into interferometers is a rare case where a quantum-optics idea directly improves a major measurement instrument. Caves's proposal and the later experimental implementation have lasting impact on gravitational-wave detectors and quantum metrology.
assessment.attribution: Caves provided the theoretical proposal, Kimble's group made an early experimental squeezing demonstration, and Schnabel and others developed the practical implementation in GEO600 and elsewhere. Mavalvala's contribution to the LIGO squeezing programme is also significant, and I could not justify a clean three-name selection with confidence.
assessment.maturity: Squeezing is routinely used in LIGO, Virgo and GEO600, so confirmation is strong. Part of the credit is tied to LIGO, which was already recognised by the 2017 prize.
uncertainties: Credit is spread over theory, early squeezing experiments and gravitational-wave implementation.
Possible perception of overlap with the 2017 LIGO prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays opens a new frequency band and is important for the physics of supermassive black-hole binaries and possibly the early universe. The experimental technique of precision pulsar timing is demanding and original.
assessment.attribution: The result comes from several large collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA) and the supplied three names cannot represent them fairly. Selecting individuals would be difficult and the claim about decisive contributors is unclear to me.
assessment.maturity: The 2023 evidence is at roughly the few-sigma level and is not yet a decisive detection of a gravitational-wave background with the expected Hellings-Downs correlation. The origin of the signal is also not yet settled, so recognition looks premature, though promising.
uncertainties: Detection significance is still modest and independent confirmation is ongoing.
Astrophysical versus cosmological origin of the signal is open.
Credit across four or more collaborations is hard to assign to three people.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon microstrip and hybrid pixel detectors enabled precision vertexing and tracking in high-rate collider environments and also have applications beyond particle physics. As an instrument builder I value detector inventions that make whole classes of measurement possible, and this one underpins the discoveries at the LHC and elsewhere.
assessment.attribution: Parker developed microstrip detectors, while Heijne and Jarron are associated with hybrid pixel concepts at CERN. The three names plausibly span the two technologies, but I am not certain that they are the decisive contributors, since other groups made major contributions to sensor and readout design.
assessment.maturity: The technology has been used for decades and is widely validated. Recognition would be late rather than premature, and the question is whether an enabling instrument invention is the intended kind of discovery or invention under the prize criteria.
uncertainties: Dispersed credit among many sensor and readout developers.
Whether the enabling-technology character is judged sufficiently fundamental for a physics prize.
My own recollection of the history of these technologies is imperfect and not independently checked here.
